definition: A value collected now and committed by a separate, later act. The only control here with three values, and no click reaches the third.
reachForItWhen: The user picks any number of options from a set and a Save or Generate button commits them.
A clip, file or row needs a selection that a bulk action reads afterwards.
A table header governs rows that are individually selectable — the one place mixed is legal.
The user accepts terms whose full text is on the screen and stays on it.

reachForSomethingElseWhen.situation: The setting applies the moment it is toggled, with no Save step
reachForSomethingElseWhen.instead: Switch, whose whole contract is immediate effect — a checkbox here promises a commit that never arrives

reachForSomethingElseWhen.situation: Exactly one option out of several is legal
reachForSomethingElseWhen.instead: No radio recipe exists. Add one under `showcase/lib/recipes/` with its own `MotionSpec` — a checkbox group enforces nothing and lets the user pick two

reachForSomethingElseWhen.situation: The selection belongs to the whole row rather than to one cell
reachForSomethingElseWhen.instead: Table, whose row variant binds `aria-selected` and `fill/selected`; a checkbox inside such a row is decoration

reachForSomethingElseWhen.situation: The tick is the action itself rather than a value collected for one
reachForSomethingElseWhen.instead: Button — the destructive variant where the action cannot be undone

variants.useWhen: Every option the user has not acted on. First in the recipe's order, so it is what renders with neither `checked` nor `defaultChecked` passed.
variants.avoidWhen: Standing in for a setting that is off and applies on click. That is Switch's off state, and this variant promises a Save step the screen does not have.

variants.useWhen: The value is already true in the data at render — a saved preference, or a row a pending bulk action already covers.
variants.avoidWhen: Pre-ticking an option that costs the user money, storage or data. A pre-ticked box records an agreement indistinguishable afterwards from one the user made.

variants.useWhen: At most one per set, and always the governing control: the header or parent whose members are split, never a member.
variants.avoidWhen: As a value the user picks, or as a half-loaded indicator. No click produces mixed, and rows that have not loaded are Skeleton's.

guidance.useWhen: Always. One size, and `sizeClasses.md` is empty — nothing in the class string varies with it.

sizes.note: The 44px touch target (`--oz-target-min`) comes from the labelled row, not from the box, so a larger box would buy no target. A smaller one is unavailable for a different reason: the tick is a token at `--oz-space-4` (12px) and the box interior is 14px — `--oz-space-5` (16px) less two `--oz-stroke-2` strokes of 1px each — so dropping the box one step crops the tick instead of scaling it.

copy: Label copy: state what is true when the box is ticked, in sentence case with no terminal full stop — accept `Add a watermark`, reject `Watermark`, a noun that says nothing about the tick
Label copy: keep the verb out of Switch's register — reject `Enable upscaling to 4K`, which claims the setting already applies, accept `Upscale to 4K on export`
Label copy: never a negation, because the user inverts twice at reading speed and gets it wrong — reject `Do not keep the source file after export`, accept `Keep the source file after export`

Label copy: never a destructive verb, because the tick then commits the deletion instead of collecting a value for one — reject `Delete source clips after export`, accept `Keep the source file after export`

Label copy: name the count and the set on a select-all — accept `Select all 12 clips`, reject `Select all`, which does not say whether all is the twelve clips on screen or the four hundred behind the filter

Label copy: put the reason inside a disabled label — the shipped string is `Commercial licence (required, locked)`, because `<button disabled>` leaves the tab order and a keyboard user never reaches the control that would otherwise carry it

No second slot: the component renders one author string. There is no description, helper or message slot in the recipe, and that is answered rather than missing — a checkbox needing a sentence of explanation has the wrong label, and the explanation goes above the group as body copy.

Fallback name: `aria-label` falls back to the string `Select` when `label` is absent. It exists so an unlabelled box is not nameless; it is not a name, and a select-all shipping it announces `Select, checkbox, mixed`, which names neither the set nor what is mixed in it.
motion: Nothing about the box moves. A press-scale here would cost more than it does on a button: the checkbox is the one control operated as a column, and a target that shrinks under the pointer at row four moves the row-five target the user is already reaching for. `enter: 'none'` is the box saying it has nothing to arrive from — it was on screen before the click, and the state change is the whole event.

behaviourUnderPressure.case: A label longer than its column
behaviourUnderPressure.behaviour: Wrap and grow past the 44px floor. Never truncate: the label is the only place the commitment is written, so the user ticks `Keep the source file after ex…` and the record says they agreed to it. `items-center` centres the box against the whole block, so beside a three-line label it sits level with line two.

behaviourUnderPressure.case: A select-all header over an empty set
behaviourUnderPressure.behaviour: Refuse mixed and render `unchecked` and `disabled` instead. Mixed over zero rows claims some of nothing is selected, and `Select all 12 clips` has no legal form at 0.

The box carries no signal and the label carries all of it. `fill/secondary-disabled` composites to 1.08:1 against a white page and the disabled stroke to 1.09:1 over that fill; on a dark dialog the same fill composites to 1.19:1 against its bed. Ship the reason in the string.

Refuse. The recipe binds base, hover, disabled and focus and no pending state, so nothing sits on screen between the tick and the response and the user ticks a second time. Leave the request on the Save or Generate button the checkbox feeds.

behaviourUnderPressure.case: A label translated to roughly 1.3× its English length
behaviourUnderPressure.behaviour: Wrap. The 16px box, the 12px gap and the 44px floor are tokens and hold in every locale, so line count is the only variable. The string that does not survive a length pass is the select-all: `Select all 12 clips` needs its count interpolated by the locale layer, because a concatenated number takes the wrong plural in Polish and Russian.

enforced.claim: The tick clears APCA Lc 60 on the brand fill in both modes and on hover — Lc 66.73 base, 77.83 light and 63.62 dark on hover. It is gated on Lc, not on the 3.55:1 WCAG ratio axe will report; DECISIONS.md H1 is the tie-breaker.
enforced.assertion: `APCA_ASSERTIONS` in `build/spec.mjs` for the token pair, and the `content-on-*` branch of `showcase/scripts/verify-contrast.ts` for the pairing the recipe creates.

enforced.claim: Every token name in the three bindings resolves in both modes. A typo fails the run rather than rendering one silently unstyled state.
A click can never produce `mixed`, so a header that unchecks from mixed is a caller reimplementing the component.
enforced.assertion: `toggle()` in `Checkbox.tsx` computes `value === true ? false : true`; `onCheckedChange` is typed `(checked: boolean) => void` and `defaultChecked` is `boolean`, so mixed is controlled-only.

enforced.claim: The box's colour change cannot be given a spring that overshoots — an overshoot on a colour clips at the channel boundary and buys a stall.
The checkbox cannot be made motionless while it binds hover.
enforced.assertion: check 3 of `showcase/scripts/verify-motion.ts`, which sweeps every bound interactive state rather than hover alone.

enforced.claim: In dark mode the bed under a checkbox in a dialog sits above `surface/tertiary`, at ΔL 0.0433 against a 0.03 floor.
enforced.assertion: the `SURFACE_LADDER` monotonicity gate in `build/build.mjs`, dark only — the four rungs are in `reports/audit.json` under `kind: 'ladder'`.

enforced.claim: The label's colour pair is gated on a floating surface: `content/secondary` on `surface/elevated` measures 6.54:1 dark against a 4.5 floor.
enforced.assertion: `CONTRAST_ASSERTIONS` in `build/spec.mjs`, six pairs added by B18b. The pair is gated; the component's use of it is not — see the first line below.

notEnforced: The label's colour is a literal `text-content-secondary` in `Checkbox.tsx`, outside `bindings`. `recipe.bindingRoles` never yields it, so no component sweep measures it, and swapping it at the call site fails nothing.

The unchecked variant creates no measured pairing at all. `verify-contrast.ts` runs `if (!merged.fg || !merged.bg) continue;` and unchecked binds no `fg` in base, hover or disabled — the box a user sees most often is measured by nothing.

`VISIBILITY_ASSERTIONS` names `border/tertiary` against `color/surface/primary` only, at a 1.6 floor. The box's stroke actually sits on `surface/primary-variant` — 1.81:1 light, 4.57:1 dark — and against a dark dialog it measures 2.77:1. Neither pair is named; adding them goes in `build/spec.mjs`, per CLAUDE.md rule 3.

The tick's spring is a class in `Checkbox.tsx`. `verify-motion.ts` sweeps `lib/core/Recipe.ts` and `lib/recipes/*.recipe.ts` and nothing else, so a hand-written `scale-[0.96]` in that file would pass every gate and keep moving for a user who asked it not to — the shape of B19, in a file the sweep B19 added does not reach.

Nothing checks that a `label` was passed. Without one the component returns the bare box, the 44px row never renders, and the accessible name falls back to `Select` — the failure the last copy bullet describes, shipping green.

Nothing checks that a select-all header derives its value from its rows on every render. A header holding its own boolean drifts the moment a row is toggled directly, and then reports checked while eleven of twelve clips are selected.

`border/focus` is gated against the page and `surface/primary`, not against `surface/elevated`, where it measures 4.54:1 dark — computed here, not from `reports/audit.json`. A checkbox in a dialog is the common case and the unnamed pair.
The 16px box, the 1px stroke and the 12px tick are arithmetic spread across two files. Change `h-space-5` in the recipe and nothing reports that the tick stopped fitting.

looksLikeABugButIsNot.observation: The generated motion summary reads `enter: — none`, and the tick visibly scales in on every click.
looksLikeABugButIsNot.why: The summary is compiled from `recipe.motion`, and that object describes the box. The box was on screen before the click and has no entrance to declare; the thing that enters is the tick, whose class sits on a child element and never passes through the recipe. `enter: 'none'` is an answer about the box, not a missing entrance.

looksLikeABugButIsNot.observation: `checked` and `indeterminate` are byte-identical in the binding table — same fill, same border, same tick colour, in both modes and every state.
looksLikeABugButIsNot.why: The difference is the SVG path and `aria-checked`, never colour. Collapsing them into a boolean deletes the only place `'mixed'` is declared, and the select-all header then announces `checked` while half its rows are unselected. The distinction is shape, and shape is not something the binding table can show.

looksLikeABugButIsNot.observation: The unchecked box has no fill of its own on a white page: `surface/primary-variant` is `#FFFFFF`, byte-identical to `color/background`.
looksLikeABugButIsNot.why: An opaque white rather than `transparent`, so the box keeps a white interior when it lands on a `surface/primary` card, a tinted panel or a thumbnail instead of taking the bed's colour. `COLLISION_ASSERTIONS` holds `surface/primary` apart from the page and deliberately does not name this pair.

looksLikeABugButIsNot.observation: A disabled checked box reads as a tick floating with no square behind it.
looksLikeABugButIsNot.why: `fill/brand-disabled` measures 1.23:1 against a white page while the tick on it measures 3.47:1, so the tick carries the whole signal and the fill carries none. A control you cannot act on keeps no role colour — I5 — and removing the tick to match the fill would delete the only readable part of the state.

related.difference: When both sit in one settings panel, colour cannot separate them — `on` and `checked` both bind `fill/brand`, so the shape and the label's verb carry the whole contract.

When the row is already selectable, a box inside it is a second copy of the selection — one `selectedKeys` prop drives both the row's fill and its announcement, and the box's own boolean is a third value nothing reconciles.
When the option is an open string rather than one of an enumerated set, there is no value here to bind it to.
When the rows a select-all governs have not arrived, the region is named once — `SkeletonGroup` takes a required `label` and marks itself `aria-busy`, where a column of boxes announces one at a time.
When exactly one option is legal, the keyboard pays too — twelve boxes are twelve tab stops where a radio group is one, and the exit is a new recipe in `showcase/lib/recipes/`.

changed.what: 2026-08-01 — a checkbox on a dark dialog now sits on a lighter bed. Its stroke measures 2.77:1 against `surface/elevated` where it measured 3.84:1, and its fill separates from that bed at 1.65:1 where it measured 1.19:1.
changed.why: DECISIONS.md B18. Both floating surfaces were `neutral/120`, byte-identical to `surface/secondary`, so the box's 1px stroke was the entire boundary; `neutral/105` (`#393735`, L* 33.8) gives the bed part of that job and takes some from the stroke. Neither pair is asserted, so measure before moving `border/tertiary`.

changed.what: 2026-08-01 — the disabled checked tick measures 4.92:1 in dark. Guidance quoting 3.82:1 is reading a fill that no longer exists. Light is unchanged at 3.47:1.
changed.why: DECISIONS.md B18c moved `fill/*-disabled` to `neutral/115` (`#272524`) after the floating surfaces took `neutral/105`. `reports/audit.json` carries 4.92; I5's prose still says 3.82:1 and has not been reconciled, so the audit wins.

changed.what: 2026-08-01 — the tick is 12px inside a 14px interior. Earlier guidance called the interior 12px and derived the tick from it.
changed.why: `border-2` resolves to `--oz-stroke-2`, which is 1px, not 2px — the ordinal stroke scale is remapped in `dist/tailwind.tokens.js`. The derivation was invented to make a token value look computed; the arithmetic that replaces it is in Sizes. CLAUDE.md rule 5.

changed.what: 2026-08-01 — B19's press-scale fix changes nothing to act on here, and the sweep shipped with it does not reach this component's tick.
changed.why: `Recipe.motionClasses` now routes a press through the multiplier, and `checkbox.recipe.ts` declares no press. The tick's scale is graded because `.oz-enter-pop` is a token-layer class, not because a gate checks it — do not add a second multiplier by hand.
